decks.module: Knowledge, vision and road test rules and retake waits
decks.domain: Licensing, permits and the driving tests

cards.front: How does a hearing impaired applicant get an interpreter, and how is the relay service reached?
cards.back: A hearing impaired applicant will be provided an interpreter if one is requested when the appointment is scheduled, and the Vermont Relay Service for text telephone users is reached by calling seven one one.

cards.front: What abilities and attitudes do the driving tests evaluate?
cards.back: The driving tests check whether you can read road signs and lights, know the state's driving laws, see well enough to drive safely, have safe and courteous driving skills, have any disability affecting safe operation, will maintain your vehicle and will respect bicyclists, motorcyclists, pedestrians and other drivers.

cards.front: What vision standard applies, and what happens if an applicant falls short?
cards.back: The vision screening checks whether your sight meets the required standard of twenty forty, and an applicant who does not meet it is referred, at their own expense, to a licensed optometrist or ophthalmologist who evaluates whether any restrictions belong on the driving privilege.

cards.front: How is the knowledge test given, how many questions does it have, and how many must be correct?
cards.back: The knowledge test is taken online and has twenty questions, each with four answer choices of which only one is correct, and you must answer at least sixteen questions correctly to pass.
cards.memory_hook: Knowledge test questions and passing count

cards.front: How long must you wait to retake a failed knowledge test?
cards.back: An applicant who fails the knowledge test must wait at least one day before taking it again.
cards.memory_hook: Wait after failing the knowledge test

cards.front: When is the road test given, and how much driving experience should precede it?
cards.back: The road test is given only after every other part of the test has been passed, and the handbook expects at least forty hours of real driving experience beforehand, guided by an experienced driver or instructor, with at least five of those hours in traffic.

cards.front: What happens during the road test, and what is not allowed in the vehicle?
cards.back: During the road test you will never be asked to do anything against the law and no tricks are played, you must follow the directions of the examiner riding with you, handle the vehicle with skill, drive at proper speeds for conditions and obey signs and rules, and no animals are allowed in the vehicle.

cards.front: How long must you wait after failing the road test once, and after three failures?
cards.back: Failing the road test means waiting at least one week before another try, and after a third failed road test the minimum wait rises to one month.
cards.memory_hook: Waits after failing the road test

cards.front: How do the retake waits differ between the road test and the knowledge test?
cards.back: A failed road test brings a one week wait, but a third failure raises the wait to at least one month, and neither matches the one day wait after a failed knowledge test.
cards.memory_hook: Road test waits versus knowledge test

decks.module: Junior license restrictions and passenger stages
decks.domain: Licensing, permits and the driving tests

cards.front: What does a student who passes a school road test receive, and what must be submitted to get the license?
cards.back: A student who passes a high school instructor's road test gets a Driver Education Examination Certificate, and the license is issued only after that certificate, a valid learner's permit, a parent-signed application, the fees and proof of Vermont residency are handed in at a motor vehicle customer service office.
cards.memory_hook: Certificate from a school road test

cards.front: On what grounds can a junior driver's license be taken away?
cards.back: A junior driver's license is a provisional license: the Commissioner of Motor Vehicles may take it away when your actions show you are an unsafe driver, and it can also be taken away when your parent or guardian withdraws permission for you to drive.

cards.front: How long may a junior license holder not drive for work, and what else is barred?
cards.back: A junior license holder may not drive a vehicle in the course of employment, such as delivering pizza, until the junior license has been held for one year or the holder turns eighteen, whichever comes first, and may never carry passengers for hire.
cards.memory_hook: No work driving on a junior

cards.front: What passenger rule applies in the first three months of a junior license?
cards.back: During the first three months on a junior driver's license the holder must drive alone unless a qualified supervisor is in the front seat, the same parent, guardian, instructor or licensed person at least twenty-five years old who may supervise a permit holder, and with one present the only passenger limit is the number of safety belts.

cards.front: What are the three passenger stages of a junior license?
cards.back: The junior license passenger rules move in three steps: driving alone for the first three months, family members during the second three months, and no passenger limit after six months, with the safety belt count capping every step.

cards.front: How do the junior license passenger rules change after three and after six months?
cards.back: During the second three months on a junior driver's license the holder may begin transporting family members, and after six months there is no limit on passengers, but at every stage the driver may never carry more passengers than there are safety belts.
cards.memory_hook: Second three months and six months

cards.front: What does the ban on portable electronic devices while driving cover?
cards.back: No driver may use any portable electronic device while operating a motor vehicle, which includes reading and manually composing or sending texts, instant messages and emails, and the devices covered include cellular phones, personal digital assistants, tablets and laptop computers.

cards.front: Who gets a full driver's license and what vehicles does it exclude?
cards.back: A driver's license is issued to eligible people aged eighteen or older who pass the required examination, and it allows driving any noncommercial vehicle except a school bus or a motorcycle, each of which needs additional exams.

cards.front: What must a permit holder bring to the road test for a full driver's license?
cards.back: For the full license road test a permit holder brings a qualified supervisor whose license is valid that day, the same parent, guardian, instructor or licensed person at least twenty-five years old who may supervise a permit holder, plus proof of insurance and registration for a sound, inspected vehicle with a working parking brake.
cards.memory_hook: Road test for a full license

decks.module: Driver education, practice hours and the night definition
decks.domain: Licensing, permits and the driving tests

cards.front: How long must a permit be held and how long must the record be clean before a junior license?
cards.back: To get a junior driver's license you must have held a learner's permit for at least one year and kept a clean record with no permit recalls, suspensions or revocations during the six months before applying.

cards.front: How does the one year permit period differ from the six month clean record period?
cards.back: The one year a learner's permit must be held before a junior license is a different clock from the six month clean record period, which counts only the six months immediately before applying.
cards.memory_hook: One year held versus six months

cards.front: Who is issued a junior driver's license, and who must sign the application?
cards.back: A junior driver's license is issued to a sixteen or seventeen year old who passes the required examination, and a parent or legal guardian must sign the application to give permission for the test.

cards.front: How many classroom, behind the wheel and observation hours does driver education require?
cards.back: Before getting a license, every sixteen and seventeen year old must pass a state approved driver education and training course made up of thirty hours of classroom study, six hours of behind the wheel training and six hours of observation.

cards.front: How many practice hours are required, how many at night, and how is nighttime defined?
cards.back: On top of the driver education course, a junior license applicant must complete forty hours of driving practice with at least ten hours at night, and nighttime means the period from thirty minutes after sunset to thirty minutes before sunrise.

cards.front: How does an expired learner's permit affect eligibility for the road test?
cards.back: An applicant may take the road test on a learner's permit that has been expired for no more than three years and was renewed before the exam, but a permit expired for more than three years requires a written exam before the road test can be given.
cards.memory_hook: Expired permit and the road test

cards.front: When does driver education taken outside Vermont count?
cards.back: Driver education taken outside Vermont counts only if a certified or licensed driver education instructor taught it with both classroom and behind the wheel training, and a completion certificate not issued by a state agency needs documentation on state letterhead listing the program's minimum requirements.

cards.front: Who certifies the practice hours, with what tools, and how do they relate to course hours?
cards.back: A parent or guardian must certify the forty hours of practice driving, at least ten of them at night, using the Driving Practice Log Sheet or the RoadReady app, and the law requires those forty hours to be in addition to the six behind the wheel hours of driver education.

cards.front: Do the forty practice hours overlap with driver education behind the wheel hours?
cards.back: The forty hours of certified practice driving are counted separately from the six behind the wheel hours of the driver education course, so the two never overlap.
cards.memory_hook: Practice hours are on top of

decks.domain: Licensing, permits and the driving tests

cards.front: What does holding a license oblige a driver to do toward other road users?
cards.back: Licensing makes driving a privilege rather than a right, so a license holder must drive within the limits of the law and treat every highway user, including bicyclists, motorcyclists and pedestrians, with courtesy and consideration.

cards.front: Which six kinds of license does Vermont issue?
cards.back: Vermont issues six kinds of license: the learner's permit, the driver's license, the junior driver's license, the commercial driver's license, the enhanced driver's license and the driver's privilege card.

cards.front: How old must a Vermont resident be to take the learner's permit test, and who else may get a permit?
cards.back: A Vermont resident must be at least fifteen years old to take the learner's permit test, and a resident of another state who is enrolled in a Vermont driver education and training course can also get a Vermont learner's permit with a school letter confirming enrollment.
cards.memory_hook: Minimum age for the permit test

cards.front: Who must sign a permit application for an applicant under eighteen, and who may not sign for an exchange student?
cards.back: A permit applicant who is fifteen, sixteen or seventeen needs a parent or legal guardian to sign the application before taking the test unless the applicant is an emancipated minor, and a foreign exchange student uses a Foreign Exchange Parental Authorization form that a host parent cannot sign.

cards.front: What two things must happen before a learner's permit is issued?
cards.back: The learner's permit is issued after the applicant passes the online permit test and pays the required fees.

cards.front: What driving record must a permit applicant under eighteen show, and over what period?
cards.back: A learner's permit applicant under eighteen must have kept a clean driving record for the previous two years, and anyone with recalls, suspensions or revocations should contact the DMV because an additional waiting period may be required.

cards.front: Who must ride in the front seat when a learner's permit holder drives?
cards.back: With a valid learner's permit you may drive anywhere in Vermont at any time, provided the front seat holds a qualified supervisor: a licensed, unimpaired parent or guardian, an unimpaired licensed or certified driver education instructor, or a licensed, unimpaired person at least twenty-five years old.

cards.front: What must you do before driving in another state on a Vermont learner's permit?
cards.back: Before driving in another state on a Vermont learner's permit, check with that state's motor vehicle agency or its law enforcement whether the permit is honored there.
cards.memory_hook: Driving out of state on a

decks.domain: Licensing, permits and the driving tests

cards.front: How soon must a new resident with an out-of-state license get a Vermont license?
cards.back: A Vermont resident who plans to drive in Vermont must hold a Vermont driver's license, and a new resident arriving with a valid license from another jurisdiction must get a Vermont license within sixty days of moving in.
cards.memory_hook: Vermont license needed after moving in

cards.front: How do the residency deadlines differ for a regular license and a commercial license?
cards.back: The sixty day window to get a Vermont license after moving in applies to a regular license, while a commercial license from another state must be transferred within the shorter window of thirty days.

cards.front: How soon must a new resident transfer a commercial driver's license to Vermont?
cards.back: A person who holds a commercial driver's license from another state must transfer that commercial license to Vermont within thirty days of establishing residency.

cards.front: What must a junior license applicant provide about a Social Security number, and how is the exam arranged?
cards.back: A junior license applicant must put a Social Security number on the application, or supply a Social Security Administration letter showing ineligibility for one, and must book an exam appointment.

cards.front: What must the holder of an out-of-state junior license do to get a Vermont junior license?
cards.back: An out-of-state junior driver's license converts to a Vermont junior license by passing the required examinations, proving completion of a state approved driver education program and proving an additional forty hours of driving.

cards.front: Which instructors may give road tests, and where?
cards.back: Some DMV licensed high school driver education instructors conduct driver's license road tests, but only at schools that have enrolled in the testing program and only through instructors certified as examiners by the Department of Motor Vehicles.

cards.front: What tests does a new resident face depending on how long their out-of-state license has been expired?
cards.back: A new Vermont resident holding a valid out-of-state license, or one expired for three years or less, takes an eye examination to get a Vermont license, while a license expired for more than three years or no license at all means taking the vision, written and road tests.
cards.memory_hook: New residents with another state's license

cards.front: How does a three year expiry decide what a transferring resident must do?
cards.back: A new resident whose out-of-state license is valid or expired three years or less needs only an eye examination, while one expired more than three years must take the vision, written and road tests like a first-time applicant.

cards.front: Who is refused a Vermont license or renewal?
cards.back: A license is refused to anyone whose driving privilege is suspended, revoked or refused in any state until that action ends and written reinstatement notice arrives, to anyone the Commissioner has evidence cannot or will not drive without endangering others, and to anyone who is not a Vermont resident.
cards.memory_hook: Who cannot be issued a license

cards.front: When does an out-of-state junior license holder escape Vermont's graduated license provisions?
cards.back: A holder of an out-of-state junior driver's license who applies for a Vermont junior license stays subject to Vermont's graduated license provisions unless the other state's junior license was held for at least six months.
cards.memory_hook: Graduated rules for transferred junior licenses

decks.module: Road test vehicle and paperwork requirements
decks.domain: Licensing, permits and the driving tests

cards.front: What condition must the junior road test vehicle be in, and what paperwork prevents testing if missing?
cards.back: The vehicle brought to a junior license road test must be clean, in good mechanical condition, legal, carry a valid inspection sticker and have a properly working emergency or parking brake, and failing to show a valid insurance card and registration certificate prevents testing.

cards.front: What information must the insurance card shown at a road test contain?
cards.back: The insurance card shown at a road test must state the name of the insurance carrier, the effective and expiration dates of coverage, the name of the insured and a description of the vehicle including its vehicle identification number.
cards.memory_hook: What the insurance card must show

cards.front: When does driving a school bus require a commercial driver's license?
cards.back: A school bus with a gross vehicle weight rating of twenty-six thousand one pounds or more, or built for sixteen or more passengers including the driver, requires a commercial driver's license with passenger and school bus endorsements.
cards.memory_hook: Large school buses need a commercial

cards.front: When does a school bus need a Type Two endorsement rather than a commercial license?
cards.back: A Type Two school bus endorsement on a regular license covers buses rated for fewer than sixteen passengers, while sixteen or more passengers or a heavy weight rating moves the driver into commercial licensing with passenger and school bus endorsements.
cards.memory_hook: Type Two versus commercial school bus

cards.front: Which ways of transporting school children require a school bus endorsement?
cards.back: A school bus endorsement is required to transport school children for hire, such as in a taxi, or in a multifunction school activity bus owned or leased by a school, and may also be required when carrying school children in privately or school owned cars and vans.
cards.memory_hook: When a school bus endorsement is

cards.front: Who may get a motorcycle endorsement, and what does the Basic Rider Course exempt?
cards.back: Any licensed person aged sixteen or older may get a motorcycle endorsement or motorcycle permit by passing a test, and students who complete the Basic Rider Course of the Vermont Rider Education Program are exempt from the state written and skill exams for the endorsement.

cards.front: How are DMV visits arranged, and what should you do if you cannot keep one?
cards.back: All DMV visits are by appointment only, scheduled through the DMV website, and an applicant who cannot keep an appointment should cancel or reschedule as soon as possible so the time can go to someone else.

cards.front: What vehicle may be used for the road test, and when are rental or dealer vehicles accepted?
cards.back: You must furnish a registered, inspected and insured vehicle for the road test from any state, a rental vehicle is accepted only when the rental company provides a letter accepting full responsibility, and a vehicle on dealer registration is accepted only for an immediate family member of the dealership.
cards.memory_hook: Vehicles accepted for the road test

cards.front: Which registration plates disqualify a vehicle from the road test, and why?
cards.back: No road test is given in a vehicle displaying agriculture, antique or exhibit plates, because the law restricts how those plates may be used.
cards.memory_hook: Restricted plates bar the road test

cards.front: What equipment must a road test vehicle have?
cards.back: A road test vehicle needs working headlights, horn, wipers, rearview mirror, tail lights, tires, steering, windshield, exhaust, brakes, fenders and bumpers, plus directional signals on vehicles made after the start of nineteen fifty-five and safety belts and defrosters on models from nineteen sixty-four on.
cards.memory_hook: Required equipment on the test vehicle

cards.front: What must the parking brake of a road test vehicle do, and what tint rule applies?
cards.back: The emergency or parking brake of a road test vehicle must be able to hold it in neutral on any grade where it is operated, both headed uphill and downhill, and illegal tinting of the front windows is not allowed.

cards.front: What endorsement is needed to carry school children in a bus rated under sixteen passengers?
cards.back: Carrying school children in a school bus the manufacturer rates for fewer than sixteen passengers requires a Type Two school bus endorsement on the regular driver's license.
cards.memory_hook: Small school buses and the Type

cards.front: Can a road test be given in a vehicle without safety belts?
cards.back: No road test is given in a vehicle that does not have safety belts.
cards.memory_hook: No safety belts, no road test
